examples: Give short and clear emergency instructions.
Emergency instructions are directions people must follow during danger or urgent situations.
“Please use the nearest safe staircase” is a clear emergency instruction.
Good emergency instructions help people move safely and avoid confusion.
In an emergency, give one instruction at a time so people can follow it quickly.
examples_zh: 發出簡短清楚的緊急指示。
緊急指示是人在危險或緊急情況下必須跟從的指示。
「請使用最近的安全樓梯」是一句清楚的緊急指示。
良好的緊急指示可幫助人們安全行動，避免混亂。
緊急情況下，每次只給一個指示，讓人可以快速跟從。

examples: Report an incident using what happened, where, when, who and action taken.
To report an incident means to give clear facts about an accident or unusual event.
Security staff should report an incident if a person collapses near the lift lobby.
A good report helps the management team understand the problem and respond correctly.
When you report an incident, include facts only and avoid guessing.
examples_zh: 匯報事故時，說明發生了甚麼、地點、時間、涉及人士及已採取的行動。
匯報事故是指清楚說明意外或異常事件的事實。
如果有人在升降機大堂附近暈倒，保安人員應匯報事故。
良好的匯報可幫助管理團隊了解問題並作出正確應對。
匯報事故時，只應包括事實，避免猜測。

examples: Report an incident using what happened, where, when, who and action taken.
Action taken means what staff have already done after the incident happened.
The action taken was to keep people away from the wet area and call management.
Recording action taken helps the next team know what has already been handled.
Do not write action taken unless the action has really been done.
examples_zh: 匯報事故時，說明發生了甚麼、地點、時間、涉及人士及已採取的行動。
已採取的行動是指事故發生後職員已經做了甚麼。
已採取的行動是讓人遠離濕滑範圍，並聯絡管理處。
記錄已採取的行動，可讓下一個團隊知道甚麼已經處理。
除非行動真的已經完成，否則不要寫成已採取的行動。

examples: Handle a mixed scenario combining greeting, registration, complaint, phone call and emergency response.
A mixed scenario has more than one problem or task happening together.
A visitor registration may become a mixed scenario if a fire alarm starts during the process.
Mixed scenarios test whether staff can change priorities quickly.
In a mixed scenario, safety should come before routine service.
examples_zh: 處理結合問候、登記、投訴、電話及緊急應對的混合情境。
混合情境是指多於一個問題或任務同時出現。
如果訪客登記期間火警鐘響起，便可能變成混合情境。
混合情境測試職員是否能迅速改變優先次序。
在混合情境中，安全應先於一般服務。

examples: Handle a mixed scenario combining greeting, registration, complaint, phone call and emergency response.
Emergency response means the actions taken when there is danger or an urgent incident.
Telling people not to use the lift is part of an emergency response during a fire alarm.
A strong emergency response gives clear instructions and calls the right team.
Emergency response should be calm, direct and based on confirmed information.
examples_zh: 處理結合問候、登記、投訴、電話及緊急應對的混合情境。
緊急應對是指有危險或緊急事故時採取的行動。
火警鐘響起時，提醒人們不要使用升降機是緊急應對的一部分。
良好的緊急應對會提供清楚指示，並聯絡正確團隊。
緊急應對應保持冷靜、直接，並根據已確認資料。

examples: Demonstrate practical improvement through final role-play performance.
Practical improvement means getting better at doing the task in a real situation.
A student shows practical improvement when they give clearer evacuation instructions than before.
Repeated role-play can lead to practical improvement in emergency communication.
Practical improvement is shown through action, not only through memorising phrases.
examples_zh: 透過最終角色扮演表現展示實際進步。
實際進步是指在真實情境中更能做好任務。
如果學生比以前更清楚地發出疏散指示，就顯示出實際進步。
反覆角色扮演可令緊急溝通有實際進步。
實際進步是透過行動展示，而不只是背誦句子。

examples: In an emergency, use short sentences, exact locations and clear next actions.
Short sentences are easier to understand when people are nervous or in danger.
“Do not use the lift” is a short sentence with a clear safety message.
Long explanations may confuse people during an evacuation.
Use short sentences first, then give more details only when it is safe.
examples_zh: 緊急情況下，使用簡短句子、確實位置和清楚的下一步行動。
當人們緊張或身處危險時，簡短句子較容易理解。
“Do not use the lift” 是一句帶有清楚安全訊息的簡短句子。
疏散期間，冗長解釋可能令人混亂。
先使用簡短句子，安全時才補充更多詳情。

examples: In an emergency, use short sentences, exact locations and clear next actions.
Exact locations tell the team precisely where the incident is happening.
“22/F, Lift Lobby C, outside Suite 2205” is an exact location.
Without exact locations, help may go to the wrong area.
Always confirm the floor, lift lobby, suite number or nearby landmark.
examples_zh: 緊急情況下，使用簡短句子、確實位置和清楚的下一步行動。
確實位置讓團隊準確知道事故在哪裡發生。
「22樓，C升降機大堂，2205室外面」是確實位置。
沒有確實位置，救援可能會前往錯誤範圍。
應確認樓層、升降機大堂、單位號碼或附近地標。

examples: In an emergency, use short sentences, exact locations and clear next actions.
Clear next actions tell people what they should do immediately after hearing the instruction.
“Please keep the route clear” is a clear next action during a medical emergency.
Clear next actions reduce panic because people know what to do.
Avoid vague words like “wait and see” when a clear action is needed.
examples_zh: 緊急情況下，使用簡短句子、確實位置和清楚的下一步行動。
清楚的下一步行動告訴人們聽到指示後要立即做甚麼。
醫療緊急情況中，「請保持通道暢通」是清楚的下一步行動。
清楚的下一步行動可減少恐慌，因為人們知道要做甚麼。
需要清楚行動時，避免使用「等一等再看」這類含糊說法。

examples: Do not guess, argue, diagnose or promise a response time you cannot confirm.
Do not guess means you should not invent details when you are unsure.
Do not guess whether the building is safe before the authorised team confirms it.
Guessing can give people wrong information during an emergency.
If you are unsure, say you will check and update them with verified information.
examples_zh: 不要猜測、爭拗、自行判斷病情，或承諾你不能確認的回應時間。
不要猜測是指不確定時不要自行編造詳情。
在獲授權團隊確認前，不要猜測大廈是否安全。
緊急情況下，猜測可能會提供錯誤資料。
如果不確定，應說你會查詢，並以已核實資料更新對方。

examples: Do not guess, argue, diagnose or promise a response time you cannot confirm.
Do not argue means you should not fight verbally with the person, even if they are upset.
Do not argue with a visitor who insists on using the lift during an alarm.
Arguing wastes time and may increase panic or anger.
Repeat the safety instruction calmly instead of arguing.
examples_zh: 不要猜測、爭拗、自行判斷病情，或承諾你不能確認的回應時間。
不要爭拗是指即使對方不滿，也不要與對方口頭爭吵。
如果訪客在警報期間堅持使用升降機，也不要與他爭拗。
爭拗會浪費時間，也可能增加恐慌或怒氣。
應冷靜重複安全指示，而不是爭拗。

examples: Do not guess, argue, diagnose or promise a response time you cannot confirm.
Do not diagnose means you should not decide the medical cause yourself.
If someone collapses, do not diagnose the condition as a heart problem.
Staff should report what they can observe, not give a medical opinion.
Ask whether the person is conscious and breathing instead of diagnosing.
examples_zh: 不要猜測、爭拗、自行判斷病情，或承諾你不能確認的回應時間。
不要自行判斷病情，是指不要自行決定醫療原因。
如果有人暈倒，不要自行判斷為心臟問題。
職員應匯報自己能觀察到的情況，而不是提出醫療意見。
應查問傷者是否清醒及有呼吸，而不是自行判斷病情。

examples: Do not promise a response time you cannot confirm.
To promise a response time means to say when help or repair will arrive.
Do not promise a response time before the responsible team confirms it.
A false time promise can make people more frustrated later.
Say you will update them once you receive verified information.
examples_zh: 不要承諾你不能確認的回應時間。
承諾回應時間是指說明支援或維修何時會到達。
在負責團隊確認前，不要承諾回應時間。
錯誤的時間承諾可能令對方之後更加不滿。
可說收到已核實資料後會更新對方。

examples: Please stay where you are for the moment.
Stay where you are means do not move from your current position.
If there is a medical emergency, the caller may be asked to stay where they are.
This instruction helps staff find the person and control the situation.
Use this phrase only when staying there is safe.
examples_zh: 請暫時留在原位。
留在原位是指不要離開目前位置。
醫療緊急情況中，來電者可能會被要求留在原位。
這個指示可幫助職員找到對方並控制情況。
只有在留在該處安全時，才使用這個說法。

examples: Please stay where you are for the moment.
For the moment means temporarily or for now.
Please keep away from the affected area for the moment.
This phrase shows that the instruction may change after more information is received.
Use “for the moment” when giving a temporary safety instruction.
examples_zh: 請暫時留在原位。
For the moment 的意思是暫時或目前。
請暫時遠離受影響範圍。
這句表示收到更多資料後，指示可能會改變。
發出臨時安全指示時，可使用 “for the moment”。

examples: Please keep away from the affected area.
Keep away from means stay at a distance from something unsafe.
Please keep away from the wet floor near the lift lobby.
Keeping people away from danger reduces the chance of injury.
Use this phrase when people should not enter or approach an area.
examples_zh: 請遠離受影響範圍。
Keep away from 是指與不安全的事物保持距離。
請遠離升降機大堂附近的濕滑地面。
讓人遠離危險，可減少受傷機會。
當人們不應進入或接近某範圍時，可使用這句。

examples: Please keep away from the affected area.
The affected area is the place directly involved in the incident.
If water is leaking from the ceiling, the wet floor is part of the affected area.
People should not walk through the affected area until it is safe.
When reporting, describe the affected area clearly and exactly.
examples_zh: 請遠離受影響範圍。
受影響範圍是直接涉及事故的地方。
如果天花漏水，濕滑地面就是受影響範圍的一部分。
在安全前，人們不應穿過受影響範圍。
匯報時，應清楚準確地描述受影響範圍。

examples: Please use the nearest safe staircase.
The nearest safe staircase is the closest staircase that can be used safely.
During a fire alarm, visitors should use the nearest safe staircase instead of the lift.
Using the nearest safe staircase helps people evacuate without delay.
Do not name a staircase unless you know it is safe to use.
examples_zh: 請使用最近的安全樓梯。
最近的安全樓梯是最近而可安全使用的樓梯。
火警鐘響起時，訪客應使用最近的安全樓梯，而不是升降機。
使用最近的安全樓梯可幫助人們盡快疏散。
除非知道該樓梯可安全使用，否則不要指定樓梯名稱。

examples: Do not use the lift.
Do not use the lift means people should not take the elevator in that situation.
During a fire alarm, staff should clearly say, “Do not use the lift.”
Lifts may be unsafe or unavailable during an emergency.
Give the alternative instruction: use the nearest safe staircase.
examples_zh: 切勿使用升降機。
Do not use the lift 是指在該情況下不要乘搭升降機。
火警鐘響起時，職員應清楚說：「切勿使用升降機。」
緊急情況下，升降機可能不安全或不能使用。
應同時給出替代指示：使用最近的安全樓梯。

examples: Please follow the evacuation signs and staff instructions.
Evacuation signs show people where to go during an emergency.
Green exit signs can guide visitors toward the nearest safe staircase.
Following evacuation signs helps people leave without needing long explanations.
If someone is unsure, tell them to follow the signs and staff directions.
examples_zh: 請依照疏散指示牌及職員指示。
疏散指示牌顯示人們在緊急情況下應前往哪裡。
綠色出口指示牌可引導訪客前往最近的安全樓梯。
跟從疏散指示牌可幫助人們離開，而不需要長篇解釋。
如果有人不確定，請叫他跟從指示牌和職員指示。

examples: Please follow the evacuation signs and staff instructions.
Staff instructions are directions given by trained staff during a situation.
Visitors should follow staff instructions during an evacuation.
Staff instructions help control movement and reduce risk.
Give staff instructions clearly and repeat them if people are confused.
examples_zh: 請依照疏散指示牌及職員指示。
職員指示是受訓職員在情況中給出的指引。
疏散期間，訪客應跟從職員指示。
職員指示有助控制人流並減低風險。
應清楚發出職員指示；如有人混亂，應重複指示。

examples: May I confirm the exact floor, suite, lift number or area?
The exact floor tells staff which level the incident is on.
“22/F” is clearer than saying “upstairs.”
Without the exact floor, the emergency team may lose time searching.
Always confirm the exact floor before reporting a building incident.
examples_zh: 請問可否確認確實樓層、單位、升降機編號或位置？
確實樓層告訴職員事故位於哪一層。
「22樓」比說「樓上」更清楚。
沒有確實樓層，緊急團隊可能會浪費時間尋找。
匯報大廈事故前，應先確認確實樓層。

examples: May I confirm the exact floor, suite, lift number or area?
A suite is an office or unit inside a building.
“Outside Suite 2205” gives a clear location for the medical emergency.
Suite numbers help staff find the incident faster on a large floor.
Ask for the nearest suite if the person cannot describe the area clearly.
examples_zh: 請問可否確認確實樓層、單位、升降機編號或位置？
單位是大廈內的辦公室或房間。
「2205室外面」為醫療緊急情況提供清楚位置。
在大型樓層中，單位號碼可幫助職員更快找到事故位置。
如果對方不能清楚描述位置，可查問最近的單位。

examples: May I confirm the exact floor, suite, lift number or area?
The lift number identifies which lift is involved.
“Lift H” is a useful lift number in a lift entrapment report.
Without the lift number, the technical team may check the wrong lift.
Ask passengers whether they can see the lift number before reporting.
examples_zh: 請問可否確認確實樓層、單位、升降機編號或位置？
升降機編號可指出涉及哪一部升降機。
「H升降機」是升降機困人匯報中的有用編號。
沒有升降機編號，技術團隊可能會檢查錯誤升降機。
匯報前，應查問乘客能否看到升降機編號。

examples: Which entrance, staircase or lift lobby are you at?
Entrance, staircase and lift lobby are location points that help staff find someone.
“Lift Lobby C” is more useful than saying “near the lifts.”
Exact location points help emergency teams reach the correct area quickly.
Ask this question when the caller gives only a general location.
examples_zh: 你在哪個入口、樓梯或升降機大堂？
入口、樓梯和升降機大堂都是幫助職員找到人的位置點。
「C升降機大堂」比說「升降機附近」更有用。
準確位置點可幫助緊急團隊快速到達正確範圍。
當來電者只提供大概位置時，可問這個問題。

examples: I’m contacting the emergency / management team now.
The emergency or management team is the group responsible for handling urgent building incidents.
Security staff may contact the emergency team after a person collapses.
Contacting the right team helps the incident receive proper support.
Tell the caller which team you are contacting so they know help is being arranged.
examples_zh: 我現在聯絡緊急支援／管理團隊。
緊急支援或管理團隊是負責處理大廈緊急事故的團隊。
有人暈倒後，保安人員可能會聯絡緊急支援團隊。
聯絡正確團隊可讓事故得到適當支援。
告訴來電者你正在聯絡哪個團隊，讓對方知道支援正在安排。

examples: I’ll give them your exact location and the information you have provided.
An exact location is the precise place where help is needed.
“18/F, rear service corridor beside the pantry” is an exact location.
Giving the exact location helps the responding team arrive faster.
Confirm the exact location before you escalate the incident.
examples_zh: 我會向他們提供您的確實位置和您提供的資料。
確實位置是需要支援的準確地點。
「18樓，茶水間旁邊的後勤服務走廊」是確實位置。
提供確實位置可幫助到場處理團隊更快到達。
升級匯報事故前，應先確認確實位置。

examples: I’ll give them your exact location and the information you have provided.
Information you have provided means the details already given by the caller or reporter.
The information you have provided includes the floor, lift lobby and person’s condition.
Passing on this information helps the next team understand the case.
Repeat key information to check it is accurate before reporting.
examples_zh: 我會向他們提供您的確實位置和您提供的資料。
您提供的資料是指來電者或匯報者已經說出的詳情。
您提供的資料包括樓層、升降機大堂和傷者情況。
轉交這些資料可幫助下一個團隊了解個案。
匯報前，應重複重點資料以確認準確。

examples: Is the person conscious and breathing?
Conscious and breathing means the person is awake or responsive and is able to breathe.
In a medical emergency, staff may ask whether the person is conscious and breathing.
This information helps emergency services understand the seriousness of the situation.
Ask what the caller can observe, but do not diagnose the condition.
examples_zh: 傷者是否清醒及有呼吸？
清醒及有呼吸是指對方醒着或有反應，並能呼吸。
醫療緊急情況中，職員可能會問傷者是否清醒及有呼吸。
這項資料可幫助緊急服務了解情況嚴重程度。
應詢問來電者能觀察到的情況，但不要自行判斷病情。

examples: Please keep the access route clear while help is on the way.
Keeping the access route clear means leaving a path open for responders.
Move bags and chairs away so the access route is clear.
A clear access route helps medical or technical teams reach the person quickly.
Ask people not to crowd around the incident area.
examples_zh: 救援人員正在趕來，請保持通道暢通。
保持通道暢通是指留出一條可供到場人員進入的路線。
移開袋和椅子，讓通道保持暢通。
通道暢通可幫助醫療或技術團隊快速到達傷者身邊。
應請其他人不要圍在事故範圍。

examples: Please keep the access route clear while help is on the way.
Help is on the way means the support team has been contacted and is coming.
Help is on the way, so please stay calm and keep the route clear.
This phrase reassures people without promising an exact arrival time.
Use it only after support has really been requested.
examples_zh: 支援正在趕來，請保持通道暢通。
Help is on the way 是指支援團隊已被聯絡並正在前來。
支援正在趕來，請保持冷靜並保持通道暢通。
這句可安撫對方，同時不承諾確實到達時間。
只有在支援真的已經被要求後，才使用這句。

examples: I’ve reported the lift entrapment and asked for urgent assistance.
Lift entrapment means people are trapped inside a lift that cannot open or move normally.
A lift entrapment should be reported with the lift number and location.
People inside a lift entrapment should not force the doors open.
During lift entrapment, stay in contact with the passengers if possible.
examples_zh: 我已匯報升降機困人事件，並要求緊急支援。
升降機困人是指有人被困在不能正常開門或移動的升降機內。
匯報升降機困人時，應提供升降機編號和位置。
升降機困人時，裡面的人不應強行打開門。
升降機困人期間，如情況許可，應與乘客保持聯絡。

examples: Please remain calm and do not force the doors open.
Remain calm means stay controlled and avoid panic.
Please remain calm while we contact the responsible team.
Calm passengers can follow safety instructions more easily.
Use this phrase to reassure people before giving the next instruction.
examples_zh: 請保持冷靜，切勿強行打開升降機門。
Remain calm 是指保持鎮定，避免恐慌。
我們聯絡負責團隊期間，請保持冷靜。
冷靜的乘客較容易跟從安全指示。
在發出下一個指示前，可使用這句安撫對方。

examples: Please remain calm and do not force the doors open.
To force the doors open means to push or pull the doors open with physical effort.
Passengers should not force the doors open during a lift entrapment.
Forcing the doors open may create extra danger.
Tell passengers to stay inside and wait for trained assistance.
examples_zh: 請保持冷靜，切勿強行打開升降機門。
Force the doors open 是指用力推或拉開門。
升降機困人時，乘客不應強行打開門。
強行打開門可能造成額外危險。
應告訴乘客留在裡面，等候受訓人員支援。

examples: Help has been requested.
Help has been requested means staff have already asked the support team to attend.
Help has been requested for the stopped lift.
This phrase reassures people that the case has not been ignored.
Add what you will do next, such as staying in contact or giving updates.
examples_zh: 已要求支援。
Help has been requested 是指職員已要求支援團隊到場。
停止運作的升降機已要求支援。
這句可安撫對方，讓他知道個案沒有被忽視。
應補充下一步，例如保持聯絡或提供更新。

examples: I’ll stay in contact with you.
To stay in contact with someone means to keep communicating with them.
I’ll stay in contact with you through the intercom until help arrives.
Staying in contact can reassure passengers trapped in a lift.
Tell people to report immediately if anyone feels unwell.
examples_zh: 我會與您保持聯絡。
Stay in contact with someone 是指與某人保持溝通。
在支援到達前，我會透過對講機與您保持聯絡。
保持聯絡可安撫被困升降機內的乘客。
應提醒對方，如有人感到不適要立即通知。

examples: I can’t confirm the response time yet.
Response time means how long it will take for help or a team to respond.
Do not confirm a response time before the responsible team replies.
Wrong response times can damage trust during an emergency.
Say you will update the person once you receive verified information.
examples_zh: 我暫時未能確認回應時間。
回應時間是指支援或團隊需要多久才會作出回應。
負責團隊回覆前，不要確認回應時間。
錯誤的回應時間會在緊急情況中影響信任。
可說收到已核實資料後會通知對方。

examples: I’ll update you once I receive verified information.
Verified information is information that has been checked and confirmed.
A confirmed release time from the responsible team is verified information.
Verified information is safer than guesses during an emergency.
Wait for verified information before giving a definite update.
examples_zh: 收到已核實資料後，我會通知您最新情況。
已核實資料是已經檢查和確認的資料。
負責團隊確認的解困時間，就是已核實資料。
緊急情況下，已核實資料比猜測更安全。
提供確定更新前，應先等待已核實資料。

examples: The fire alarm is sounding.
A fire alarm warns people that there may be a fire or emergency.
When the fire alarm sounds, visitors should stop normal activities and listen to staff.
A fire alarm may require people to leave by the nearest safe staircase.
Staff should respond to a fire alarm with short, clear instructions.
examples_zh: 火警鐘正在響起。
火警鐘提醒人們可能有火警或緊急情況。
火警鐘響起時，訪客應停止一般活動並聆聽職員指示。
火警鐘響起時，人們可能需要經最近的安全樓梯離開。
職員應用簡短清楚的指示回應火警鐘。

examples: The alarm has started. Is this an evacuation?
“The alarm has started” means the warning sound has begun.
If the alarm has started, staff should not continue normal registration.
Once the alarm has started, people may need evacuation instructions.
This phrase helps report the beginning of an emergency signal.
examples_zh: 警報已響起。這是疏散嗎？
“The alarm has started” 指警報聲已經開始。
如果警報已響起，職員不應繼續一般登記程序。
警報一響起，人們可能需要疏散指示。
這句有助匯報緊急警報開始。

examples: The alarm has started. Is this an evacuation?
Evacuation means people leave a building or area for safety.
During an evacuation, do not use the lift.
Clear evacuation instructions help people leave calmly.
Evacuation should follow signs, staff directions and safe routes.
examples_zh: 警報已響起。這是疏散嗎？
疏散是指人們為安全而離開大廈或某個範圍。
疏散期間，切勿使用升降機。
清楚的疏散指示可幫助人們冷靜離開。
疏散應跟從指示牌、職員指示和安全路線。

examples: Please stay calm and follow my instructions.
To follow my instructions means to do what I tell you for safety.
Please follow my instructions and move towards the staircase.
Following instructions can reduce confusion during an alarm.
Staff should give instructions clearly before asking people to follow them.
examples_zh: 請保持冷靜，並跟從我的指示。
跟從我的指示是指為安全而按我說的去做。
請跟從我的指示，前往樓梯方向。
跟從指示可減少警報期間的混亂。
職員應先清楚發出指示，再要求人們跟從。

examples: Please remain calm and follow the evacuation instructions.
To follow the evacuation instructions means to obey the safety directions for leaving.
Visitors should follow the evacuation instructions instead of choosing their own route.
These instructions help people avoid unsafe areas.
Repeat the evacuation instructions if people look confused.
examples_zh: 請保持冷靜，並跟從疏散指示。
跟從疏散指示是指按照離開時的安全指引行動。
訪客應跟從疏散指示，而不是自行選擇路線。
這些指示可幫助人們避開不安全範圍。
如果有人看起來混亂，應重複疏散指示。

examples: Can I take the lift down?
To take the lift down means to use the elevator to go to a lower floor.
During a fire alarm, visitors should not take the lift down.
Taking the lift down may be unsafe during an emergency.
Give the safer alternative: use the nearest safe staircase.
examples_zh: 我可以乘升降機下樓嗎？
Take the lift down 是指使用升降機前往較低樓層。
火警鐘響起時，訪客不應乘升降機下樓。
緊急情況下乘升降機下樓可能不安全。
應給出較安全的替代指示：使用最近的安全樓梯。

examples: I am on a high floor.
A high floor means an upper level of a building.
People on a high floor may worry about how to evacuate safely.
Even on a high floor, visitors should not use the lift during a fire alarm.
Staff should direct people on high floors to safe staircases.
examples_zh: 我在高層。
高層是指大廈較高的樓層。
身處高層的人可能會擔心如何安全疏散。
即使在高層，火警鐘響起時也不應使用升降機。
職員應指示高層人士前往安全樓梯。

examples: Can I use the lift to leave the building?
To leave the building means to go out of the building.
During an evacuation, people leave the building by safe routes.
Staff should not tell people the building is safe before confirmation.
After people leave the building, they should follow directions to the assembly area.
examples_zh: 我可以使用升降機離開大廈嗎？
Leave the building 是指離開大廈範圍。
疏散期間，人們會經安全路線離開大廈。
在確認前，職員不應說大廈已安全。
離開大廈後，人們應按指示前往集合地點。

examples: I’m afraid not. For safety, please do not use the lift.
“I’m afraid not” is a polite way to say no.
I’m afraid not. You cannot return to the affected floor now.
This phrase helps refuse a request without sounding rude.
After saying “I’m afraid not,” give the safety reason and next step.
examples_zh: 恐怕不可以。為安全起見，請不要使用升降機。
“I’m afraid not” 是有禮貌地拒絕的說法。
恐怕不可以。您現在不能返回受影響樓層。
這句可幫助拒絕要求，同時不顯得無禮。
說完 “I’m afraid not” 後，應說明安全原因和下一步。

examples: For safety, please do not use the lift.
“For safety” explains that an instruction protects people.
For safety, please keep away from the affected area.
This phrase helps people understand why they must follow the instruction.
Use “for safety” before giving a clear emergency instruction.
examples_zh: 為安全起見，請不要使用升降機。
“For safety” 說明某個指示是為了保護人。
為安全起見，請遠離受影響範圍。
這句可幫助人們明白為何必須跟從指示。
發出清楚緊急指示前，可使用 “for safety”。

examples: Proceed by the nearest safe staircase.
“Proceed by” means go using a particular route or method.
Please proceed by the marked evacuation route.
This phrase gives a clear route without adding too much explanation.
Use “proceed by” when directing people to a safe path.
examples_zh: 請經由最近的安全樓梯離開。
“Proceed by” 是指經由某條路線或方式前往。
請經由已標示的疏散路線前往。
這句可清楚指出路線，而不需要太多解釋。
指示人們前往安全路線時，可使用 “proceed by”。

examples: Can you tell me which route to take?
Which route to take means which way someone should go.
During an evacuation, visitors may ask which route to take.
Staff should direct them to the nearest safe staircase or signage.
Do not invent a route if you are not sure it is safe.
examples_zh: 可否告訴我應該走哪條路線？
Which route to take 是指某人應該走哪條路。
疏散期間，訪客可能會問應該走哪條路線。
職員應指示他們前往最近的安全樓梯或跟從指示牌。
如果不確定路線是否安全，不要自行編造路線。

examples: Please follow the evacuation signage and staff directions.
Evacuation signage means signs that guide people during evacuation.
Exit arrows and staircase signs are evacuation signage.
Evacuation signage helps people find safe routes quickly.
Staff may say, “Please follow the evacuation signage,” when giving directions.
examples_zh: 請跟從疏散指示標誌和職員指示。
疏散指示標誌是疏散時引導人們的標誌。
出口箭咀和樓梯標誌都是疏散指示標誌。
疏散指示標誌可幫助人們快速找到安全路線。
給出方向時，職員可說：「請跟從疏散指示標誌。」

examples: Please follow the evacuation signage and staff directions.
Staff directions are instructions given by staff during the situation.
During a fire alarm, staff directions may tell visitors where to walk.
Staff directions help keep people moving in the correct direction.
Follow staff directions even if the normal route is closed.
examples_zh: 請跟從疏散指示標誌和職員指示。
職員指示是職員在情況中給出的指令。
火警鐘響起時，職員指示可能會告訴訪客往哪裡走。
職員指示可幫助人們朝正確方向前行。
即使平日路線關閉，也應跟從職員指示。

examples: Keep moving and do not run.
Keep moving means continue walking forward without stopping unnecessarily.
During evacuation, people should keep moving towards the staircase.
Keeping moving helps prevent crowding near exits.
Staff can use this phrase to keep the flow calm and steady.
examples_zh: 請繼續前行，不要奔跑。
Keep moving 是指繼續向前走，不要不必要地停下。
疏散期間，人們應繼續前往樓梯方向。
繼續前行可防止出口附近擠塞。
職員可使用這句令流動保持冷靜和穩定。

examples: Keep moving and do not run.
Do not run means people should walk instead of rushing.
During evacuation, running may cause people to fall or panic.
“Do not run” is a short safety instruction.
Pair it with a positive instruction: walk quickly.
examples_zh: 請繼續前行，不要奔跑。
Do not run 是指人們應步行，不要急跑。
疏散期間，奔跑可能令人跌倒或恐慌。
“Do not run” 是一句簡短的安全指示。
可配合正面指示使用：快步行走。

examples: Walk quickly, but do not run.
Walk quickly means move at a fast walking pace.
Visitors should walk quickly to the staircase during evacuation.
Walking quickly helps evacuation continue without causing panic.
This instruction is clearer than saying “hurry up.”
examples_zh: 請快步行走，但不要奔跑。
Walk quickly 是指以較快步速步行。
疏散期間，訪客應快步前往樓梯。
快步行走可讓疏散繼續，同時不造成恐慌。
這句比說 “hurry up” 更清楚。

examples: Can I go back to the office to get my laptop?
To go back to the office means to return to the workplace or suite.
During evacuation, people should not go back to the office for personal items.
Going back to the office may put the person in danger.
Staff should say clearly, “Please do not go back.”
examples_zh: 我可以返回辦公室拿手提電腦嗎？
Go back to the office 是指返回工作地點或單位。
疏散期間，人們不應返回辦公室取個人物品。
返回辦公室可能令對方身處危險。
職員應清楚說：「請不要回去。」

examples: I left my laptop upstairs. Can I go back for it?
To go back for it means to return somewhere to get something.
During an alarm, do not go back for a bag, phone or laptop.
Going back for it can delay evacuation.
Safety is more important than personal belongings.
examples_zh: 我把手提電腦留在樓上。可以回去取回它嗎？
Go back for it 是指返回某處取回某物。
警報期間，不要回去取袋、電話或手提電腦。
返回取回物品可能延誤疏散。
安全比個人物品更重要。

examples: Please do not go back.
Do not go back means do not return to the place you came from.
Please do not go back to the office during the evacuation.
This instruction protects people from entering a possible danger area.
Use this phrase firmly but calmly.
examples_zh: 請不要回去。
Do not go back 是指不要返回原來的地方。
疏散期間，請不要返回辦公室。
這個指示可防止人們進入可能有危險的範圍。
使用這句時，語氣應堅定但冷靜。

examples: Please do not return to the affected floor.
Do not return to means do not go back to a particular place.
Do not return to the lobby until staff confirm it is safe.
This phrase is useful when a specific area may still be unsafe.
Add the location clearly after “do not return to.”
examples_zh: 請不要返回受影響樓層。
Do not return to 是指不要回到某個指定地方。
在職員確認安全前，請不要返回大堂。
當某個特定範圍可能仍不安全時，這句很有用。
“Do not return to” 後面應清楚加上地點。

examples: Please do not return to the affected floor.
The affected floor is the floor involved in the incident or emergency.
If smoke is reported on 18/F, 18/F may be the affected floor.
People should not return to the affected floor until it is cleared.
Staff should name the affected floor only when it is confirmed.
examples_zh: 請不要返回受影響樓層。
受影響樓層是涉及事故或緊急情況的樓層。
如果18樓有煙霧報告，18樓可能是受影響樓層。
在安全確認前，人們不應返回受影響樓層。
職員只應在確認後才說明受影響樓層。

examples: Continue evacuating and follow staff instructions.
Continue evacuating means keep leaving the building or area safely.
If someone asks to go back, tell them to continue evacuating.
Continuing evacuation keeps people moving away from possible danger.
This phrase is useful when someone is distracted by belongings.
examples_zh: 請繼續疏散，並跟從職員指示。
Continue evacuating 是指繼續安全離開大廈或範圍。
如果有人要求回去，應叫他繼續疏散。
繼續疏散可讓人遠離可能的危險。
當有人因個人物品分心時，這句很有用。

examples: Please proceed to the designated assembly area as directed by staff.
A designated assembly area is the planned place where people gather after evacuation.
Staff may direct visitors to the designated assembly area outside the building.
Gathering there helps staff check people and give updates.
Do not invent an assembly area if it has not been confirmed.
examples_zh: 請按職員指示前往指定集合地點。
指定集合地點是疏散後人們集合的預定地方。
職員可能會指示訪客前往大廈外的指定集合地點。
在該處集合可幫助職員點算人員並提供更新。
如果集合地點未經確認，不要自行編造。

examples: Please proceed to the designated assembly area as directed by staff.
As directed by staff means according to the instructions given by staff.
Please leave by the safe staircase as directed by staff.
This phrase tells people to follow official on-site guidance.
It is useful when the exact route may depend on the situation.
examples_zh: 請按職員指示前往指定集合地點。
As directed by staff 是指按照職員給出的指示。
請按職員指示經安全樓梯離開。
這句告訴人們跟從現場正式指引。
當確實路線可能視乎情況而定時，這句很有用。

examples: I cannot confirm re-entry until the building gives the all-clear.
Re-entry means going back into a building or area after leaving it.
Re-entry should not happen until the authorised team confirms it is safe.
Staff should avoid promising re-entry too early.
Use this word when explaining when people may go back inside.
examples_zh: 在大廈發出安全確認前，我未能確認可否重新進入。
Re-entry 是指離開後重新進入大廈或某個範圍。
在獲授權團隊確認安全前，不應重新進入。
職員應避免太早承諾可重新進入。
解釋人們何時可以回到室內時，可使用這個詞。

examples: The authorised team gives the all-clear.
The all-clear is an official confirmation that it is safe to return or continue.
Visitors should wait outside until the all-clear is given.
Without the all-clear, people should not re-enter the building.
Staff should say who must give the all-clear if that is known.
examples_zh: 獲授權團隊發出安全確認。
All-clear 是正式確認可以安全返回或繼續。
訪客應在外面等候，直到發出安全確認。
沒有安全確認前，人們不應重新進入大廈。
如果知道，職員應說明由誰發出安全確認。

examples: Re-entry can only be confirmed after the authorised team gives the all-clear.
An authorised team is a team allowed to make official safety decisions.
Security staff may need to wait for the authorised team before confirming re-entry.
This prevents unconfirmed or unsafe instructions.
Use this phrase when explaining why you cannot make the decision yourself.
examples_zh: 只有在獲授權團隊發出安全確認後，才可確認重新進入。
獲授權團隊是有權作出正式安全決定的團隊。
保安人員可能需要等待獲授權團隊，才可確認重新進入。
這可避免未確認或不安全的指示。
解釋為何自己不能作決定時，可使用這句。

examples: We need urgent help.
Urgent help means assistance is needed immediately or very quickly.
A person who has collapsed near the lift lobby needs urgent help.
Asking for urgent help tells staff the case is serious.
Staff should collect the exact location before calling for help.
examples_zh: 我們需要緊急協助。
緊急協助是指需要立即或很快提供支援。
有人在升降機大堂附近暈倒，需要緊急協助。
要求緊急協助可讓職員知道個案嚴重。
職員應先取得確實位置，再求援。

examples: My colleague has collapsed near the lift lobby.
Has collapsed means someone has suddenly fallen down and may need help.
If a person has collapsed, ask whether they are conscious and breathing.
Do not diagnose why the person has collapsed.
Report the exact location and the observable condition.
examples_zh: 我的同事在升降機大堂附近暈倒了。
Has collapsed 是指某人突然倒下，可能需要協助。
如果有人暈倒，應查問他是否清醒及有呼吸。
不要自行判斷對方為何暈倒。
應匯報確實位置和可觀察到的情況。

examples: My colleague has collapsed near the lift lobby.
Near the lift lobby means close to the area outside the lifts.
A caller may say the person is near the lift lobby if they cannot give a suite number.
This location helps staff find the area faster.
Ask which lift lobby it is if the building has several.
examples_zh: 我的同事在升降機大堂附近暈倒了。
Near the lift lobby 是指靠近升降機外面的範圍。
如果來電者不能提供單位號碼，可能會說人在升降機大堂附近。
這個位置資料可幫助職員更快找到範圍。
如果大廈有多個升降機大堂，應查問是哪一個。

front: exact floor, lift lobby and nearest suite number
back: 確實樓層、升降機大堂及最近單位號碼
examples: May I confirm the exact floor, lift lobby and nearest suite number?
This phrase asks for three details that help locate an incident precisely.
In a medical emergency, the nearest suite number can guide responders.
Floor and lift lobby information reduce searching time.
Ask this when someone reports an incident inside a large building.
examples_zh: 請問可否確認確實樓層、升降機大堂及最近單位號碼？
這句是要求三項資料，以便準確找出事故位置。
醫療緊急情況中，最近單位號碼可引導救援人員。
樓層和升降機大堂資料可減少尋找時間。
在大型大廈內有人匯報事故時，可使用這句。

examples: Is the person awake and breathing?
Awake and breathing means the person is conscious enough to be awake and is breathing.
Ask this question when someone has collapsed.
This is an observation question, not a diagnosis.
If the caller is unsure, ask them to tell you only what they can observe.
examples_zh: 傷者是否清醒及有呼吸？
Awake and breathing 是指對方清醒並正在呼吸。
有人暈倒時，可問這個問題。
這是觀察問題，不是診斷。
如果來電者不確定，請他只說出能觀察到的情況。

examples: Is the person conscious, and are they breathing normally?
Breathing normally means breathing in a regular and not unusual way.
Staff may ask whether the person is breathing normally during a medical emergency.
This information helps responders understand the condition.
Do not describe the cause; report only what is observed.
examples_zh: 傷者是否清醒？是否正常呼吸？
Breathing normally 是指呼吸規律，沒有明顯異常。
醫療緊急情況中，職員可能會問傷者是否正常呼吸。
這項資料可幫助救援人員了解情況。
不要描述原因，只匯報觀察到的情況。

examples: Please tell me only what you can observe.
What you can observe means what you can see, hear or notice directly.
Say whether the person is breathing, moving or responding.
Observed facts are safer than guesses during an emergency.
Staff should ask for observations instead of opinions.
examples_zh: 請只告訴我你能觀察到的情況。
What you can observe 是指你能直接看見、聽見或察覺到的情況。
請說明對方是否有呼吸、移動或反應。
緊急情況下，觀察到的事實比猜測更安全。
職員應查問觀察資料，而不是意見。

examples: He is breathing, but he is not responding to us.
Not responding to us means the person does not react when people speak or try to get a response.
A person may be breathing but not responding to questions.
This should be reported clearly to the emergency team.
Do not shake or move the person unless there is immediate danger.
examples_zh: 他有呼吸，但對我們沒有反應。
Not responding to us 是指別人說話或嘗試叫他回應時，他沒有反應。
一個人可能有呼吸，但對問題沒有反應。
這項資料應清楚匯報給緊急支援團隊。
除非有即時危險，否則不要搖動或移動對方。

examples: He is breathing, but he is unresponsive.
Unresponsive means the person does not react to voice, touch or questions.
If someone is unresponsive, request emergency assistance immediately.
Use this word only when the person clearly gives no response.
Pair it with breathing information when reporting the case.
examples_zh: 他有呼吸，但沒有反應。
Unresponsive 是指對聲音、觸碰或問題沒有反應。
如果有人沒有反應，應立即要求緊急支援。
只有在對方明顯沒有回應時，才使用這個詞。
匯報時，應同時說明呼吸情況。

examples: I’ll call for emergency assistance now.
Emergency assistance is urgent help from the appropriate support team.
A collapsed person may need emergency assistance.
Calling for emergency assistance should include the exact location.
Tell the reporter what safety steps to take while help is arranged.
examples_zh: 我現在會要求緊急支援。
緊急支援是由合適支援團隊提供的緊急協助。
有人暈倒時，可能需要緊急支援。
要求緊急支援時，應包括確實位置。
安排支援期間，應告訴匯報者要採取甚麼安全步驟。

examples: I’m requesting emergency assistance now.
Requesting emergency assistance means asking the emergency team to help.
I’m requesting emergency assistance and giving them your exact location.
This phrase reassures the caller that action is being taken.
Use it only when you are actually making the request.
examples_zh: 我現在正在要求緊急支援。
Requesting emergency assistance 是指要求緊急團隊提供協助。
我正在要求緊急支援，並向他們提供您的確實位置。
這句可安撫來電者，讓對方知道行動正在進行。
只有在你真的正在提出要求時，才使用這句。

examples: Please keep the area clear.
Keep the area clear means remove people or objects from the incident space.
Please keep the area clear around the person who collapsed.
A clear area gives responders space to work.
This instruction also helps protect other people nearby.
examples_zh: 請保持範圍暢通。
Keep the area clear 是指讓人或物品離開事故範圍。
請保持暈倒人士周圍範圍暢通。
範圍暢通可讓救援人員有空間工作。
這個指示也有助保護附近其他人。

examples: Should we move him to a chair?
To move him to a chair means to lift or guide the person onto a seat.
Do not move him to a chair unless there is immediate danger or trained help advises it.
Moving someone without knowing their condition may be unsafe.
Staff should tell the caller to wait for the responding team to assess the situation.
examples_zh: 我們應否將他移到椅子上？
Move him to a chair 是指把對方扶起或移到座位上。
除非有即時危險或受訓人員建議，否則不要將他移到椅子上。
在不了解情況下移動對方可能不安全。
職員應叫來電者等候到場處理團隊評估情況。

examples: Should we move him away from the lift lobby?
Move him away from means take him to another place.
Do not move him away from the lift lobby unless there is immediate danger.
Moving a collapsed person may create extra risk.
Keep the access route clear instead of moving him unnecessarily.
examples_zh: 我們應否將他移離升降機大堂？
Move him away from 是指把他帶到另一個地方。
除非有即時危險，否則不要將他移離升降機大堂。
移動暈倒人士可能造成額外風險。
與其不必要地移動他，不如保持通道暢通。

examples: Please do not move him unless there is immediate danger.
Immediate danger means a serious risk is happening now or about to happen.
Fire, falling objects or electrical danger may be immediate danger.
If there is no immediate danger, wait for trained responders.
This phrase helps explain when moving someone may be necessary.
examples_zh: 除非有即時危險，否則請不要移動他。
即時危險是指嚴重風險正在發生或即將發生。
火警、墜物或電力危險可能是即時危險。
如果沒有即時危險，應等候受訓救援人員。
這句可解釋甚麼情況下可能需要移動人。

examples: Help is being arranged.
Help is being arranged means staff are organising support now.
Help is being arranged for the person near Lift Lobby C.
This phrase reassures the caller without giving an exact time.
Add a safety instruction while the caller waits.
examples_zh: 正在安排支援。
Help is being arranged 是指職員正在安排支援。
正在為 C 升降機大堂附近的人安排支援。
這句可安撫來電者，同時不提供確實時間。
來電者等候期間，應加上安全指示。

examples: The responding team will assess the situation on arrival.
The responding team is the group that comes to handle the incident.
The responding team may include emergency, medical, technical or management staff.
Give the responding team the exact location and known facts.
Do not promise what the responding team will decide before they arrive.
examples_zh: 到場處理團隊會在到達時評估情況。
到場處理團隊是前來處理事故的團隊。
到場處理團隊可能包括緊急支援、醫療、技術或管理人員。
應向到場處理團隊提供確實位置和已知事實。
在他們到達前，不要承諾到場處理團隊會作出甚麼決定。

examples: The responding team will assess the situation on arrival.
To assess the situation means to check what is happening before deciding what to do.
The team will assess the situation before moving the person.
Assessment helps avoid unsafe or incorrect action.
Use this phrase when the facts still need professional checking.
examples_zh: 到場處理團隊會在到達時評估情況。
Assess the situation 是指先檢查正在發生甚麼，再決定行動。
團隊會先評估情況，才移動傷者。
評估可避免不安全或錯誤的行動。
當事實仍需要專業檢查時，可使用這句。

examples: The responding team will assess the situation on arrival.
On arrival means when the team reaches the location.
The technician will check the lift on arrival.
Some decisions can only be made on arrival because the team must inspect the scene.
This phrase avoids promising action before the team gets there.
examples_zh: 到場處理團隊會在到達時評估情況。
On arrival 是指團隊到達位置時。
技術員到場時會檢查升降機。
有些決定只能在到場時作出，因為團隊必須檢查現場。
這句可避免在團隊到達前承諾行動。

examples: Stay with him if it is safe.
Stay with him means remain near the person and monitor the situation.
Stay with him if there is no danger to you.
Staying with the person can help you notice changes in condition.
Do not stay too close if the area becomes unsafe.
examples_zh: 如果安全，請留在他身邊。
Stay with him 是指留在對方附近並留意情況。
如果對你沒有危險，請留在他身邊。
留在對方身邊可幫助你留意情況變化。
如果範圍變得不安全，不要站得太近。

front: if it is safe to do so
back: 如果這樣做是安全的話
examples: Please stay with him if it is safe to do so.
If it is safe to do so means only do the action if it does not put you in danger.
Keep the route clear if it is safe to do so.
This phrase protects the helper as well as the injured person.
Use it when asking someone to help during an emergency.
examples_zh: 如果這樣做是安全的話，請留在他身邊。
If it is safe to do so 是指只有在不令自己有危險時才做。
如果這樣做是安全的話，請保持通道暢通。
這句同時保護協助者和受傷人士。
緊急情況下要求他人協助時，可使用這句。

examples: Tell me immediately if his condition changes.
Condition changes means the person’s state becomes different.
If the person stops responding or breathing changes, the condition changes.
Reporting condition changes helps responders update their response.
Ask the caller to report changes immediately, not later.
examples_zh: 如果他的情況有變，請立即告訴我。
Condition changes 是指對方的狀態出現變化。
如果對方停止反應或呼吸有變，就是情況有變。
匯報情況變化可幫助救援人員更新應對。
應要求來電者立即匯報變化，而不是稍後再說。

examples: Update me immediately if there is any change in his condition.
Any change in his condition means any new or different sign in how he is doing.
A change in breathing, response or colour may be important.
This phrase tells the caller to keep observing carefully.
Use it when help is on the way but the situation may change.
examples_zh: 如果他的情況有任何變化，請立即通知我。
Any change in his condition 是指他的狀態出現任何新變化。
呼吸、反應或面色的變化都可能很重要。
這句提醒來電者要繼續小心觀察。
當支援正在趕來而情況可能變化時，可使用這句。

examples: The lift has stopped and the doors will not open.
Lift has stopped means the elevator is no longer moving.
If the lift has stopped between floors, passengers may feel anxious.
A stopped lift should be reported with the lift number and location.
Tell passengers to remain calm and not force the doors open.
examples_zh: 升降機已停下，門不能打開。
Lift has stopped 是指升降機不再移動。
如果升降機停在樓層之間，乘客可能會感到不安。
匯報升降機停下時，應提供升降機編號和位置。
應提醒乘客保持冷靜，不要強行打開門。

examples: The lift has stopped and the doors will not open.
Doors will not open means the doors stay closed even when people expect them to open.
If lift doors will not open, passengers should not force them.
This detail helps identify a lift entrapment problem.
Report whether the doors are fully closed or partly open if known.
examples_zh: 升降機已停下，門不能打開。
Doors will not open 是指門在應該打開時仍然關着。
如果升降機門不能打開，乘客不應強行打開。
這項資料有助判斷是否屬升降機困人。
如知道，應匯報門是完全關上還是部分打開。

back: 升降機車廂停在樓層之間
examples: The car has stopped between floors and the doors are not opening.
The car means the lift compartment that carries passengers.
If the car has stopped between floors, passengers should remain inside.
This location detail is important for the technical team.
Ask which floors the car appears to be between.
examples_zh: 升降機車廂停在樓層之間，門沒有打開。
The car 是指載乘客的升降機車廂。
如果車廂停在樓層之間，乘客應留在裏面。
這項位置資料對技術團隊很重要。
應查問車廂似乎停在哪兩層之間。

examples: The doors are not opening.
Doors are not opening means the doors remain closed and cannot be used normally.
If the doors are not opening, passengers should use the intercom for help.
This phrase describes the problem without guessing the cause.
Report it together with the lift number.
examples_zh: 門沒有打開。
Doors are not opening 是指門仍然關上，不能正常使用。
如果門沒有打開，乘客應使用對講機求助。
這句描述問題，而不猜測原因。
匯報時應同時提供升降機編號。

examples: Which lift are you in?
This question asks the passenger to identify the lift involved.
Which lift are you in — Lift H or Lift G?
The answer helps the technical team find the correct lift.
Ask this early in a lift entrapment call.
examples_zh: 你在哪部升降機內？
這個問題是要求乘客指出涉及哪部升降機。
你在哪部升降機內——H升降機還是G升降機？
答案可幫助技術團隊找到正確升降機。
升降機困人通話中，應及早問這句。

examples: Can you see the lift number?
To see the lift number means to identify the lift from a sign, display or label.
Passengers may see the lift number inside the car.
The lift number helps staff report the entrapment accurately.
If they cannot see it, ask for another location clue.
examples_zh: 你能看到升降機編號嗎？
See the lift number 是指從標誌、顯示屏或標籤辨認升降機。
乘客可能在車廂內看到升降機編號。
升降機編號可幫助職員準確匯報困人事件。
如果對方看不到，應查問其他位置線索。

examples: It appears to have stopped between 17/F and 18/F.
Appears to have stopped means it seems to have stopped, based on available information.
Use this phrase when you are not fully certain but have a reasonable observation.
It sounds more careful than saying the position is definitely confirmed.
Confirm the exact information when the technical team checks the lift.
examples_zh: 它似乎停在17樓與18樓之間。
Appears to have stopped 是指根據現有資料，看起來已停下。
當你未完全確定但有合理觀察時，可使用這句。
這比直接說位置已完全確認更謹慎。
技術團隊檢查升降機時，再確認確實資料。

back: 在十七樓與十八樓之間
examples: It stopped between 17/F and 18/F.
Between 17/F and 18/F means in the space between the seventeenth and eighteenth floors.
A lift stopped between floors may require technical assistance.
This detail helps staff know where the lift car is located.
Repeat the floor information to confirm it is correct.
examples_zh: 它停在17樓與18樓之間。
Between 17/F and 18/F 是指在十七樓與十八樓之間的位置。
升降機停在樓層之間，可能需要技術支援。
這項資料可幫助職員知道車廂位置。
應重複樓層資料，以確認正確。

examples: Yes, that is correct.
That is correct means the information is accurate.
“Lift H, between 17/F and 18/F — is that correct?” “Yes, that is correct.”
This phrase helps confirm key details before reporting.
Use it when checking location, number of people or safety information.
examples_zh: 是的，正確。
That is correct 是指資料準確。
「H升降機，在17樓與18樓之間——正確嗎？」「是的，正確。」
這句有助在匯報前確認重點資料。
核對位置、人數或安全資料時，可使用這句。

examples: How many people are inside?
This question asks for the number of people in the lift or area.
In a lift entrapment, staff must know how many people are inside.
The number helps the responding team prepare properly.
Ask this before checking whether anyone is injured or unwell.
examples_zh: 裏面有多少人？
這個問題是詢問升降機或範圍內有多少人。
升降機困人時，職員必須知道裏面有多少人。
人數可幫助到場處理團隊作好準備。
應先問人數，再查問是否有人受傷或不適。

examples: How many passengers are inside?
Passengers are people travelling in a lift, vehicle or transport system.
Three passengers are trapped inside Lift H.
Knowing the number of passengers helps staff report the case clearly.
Use “passengers” when talking about people inside a lift.
examples_zh: 裏面有多少名乘客？
乘客是指乘搭升降機、車輛或交通工具的人。
三名乘客被困在H升降機內。
知道乘客人數可幫助職員清楚匯報個案。
談及升降機內的人時，可使用 “passengers”。

examples: Is anyone hurt or feeling unwell?
Hurt means injured or in pain.
Ask whether anyone is hurt during a lift entrapment.
If someone is hurt, the case may need urgent medical support.
Record the answer clearly without adding your own guess.
examples_zh: 有人受傷或感到不適嗎？
Hurt 是指受傷或感到痛楚。
升降機困人時，應查問是否有人受傷。
如果有人受傷，個案可能需要緊急醫療支援。
應清楚記錄答案，不要加入自己的猜測。

examples: Is anyone injured or feeling unwell?
Injured means physically hurt.
A passenger may be injured if they fell when the lift stopped.
Injury information helps the responding team decide what support is needed.
Use “injured” in professional reports.
examples_zh: 有人受傷或感到不適嗎？
Injured 是指身體受傷。
如果升降機停下時有人跌倒，乘客可能會受傷。
受傷資料可幫助到場處理團隊決定需要甚麼支援。
專業報告中可使用 “injured”。

examples: Is anyone injured or feeling unwell?
Feeling unwell means feeling sick, dizzy, weak or uncomfortable.
A trapped passenger may feel unwell because they are anxious or hot.
Staff should ask about feeling unwell as well as visible injury.
Report immediately if anyone starts feeling unwell.
examples_zh: 有人受傷或感到不適嗎？
Feeling unwell 是指感到不舒服、頭暈、虛弱或不適。
被困乘客可能因焦慮或悶熱而感到不適。
職員應查問是否有人感到不適，也要查問可見傷勢。
如果有人開始感到不適，應立即匯報。

examples: No one is hurt, but one person is very nervous.
Very nervous means extremely worried or frightened.
A passenger may become very nervous while trapped in a lift.
Calm communication can help a very nervous person feel safer.
Tell the person that help has been requested and stay in contact.
examples_zh: 沒有人受傷，但有一個人很緊張。
Very nervous 是指非常擔心或害怕。
乘客被困升降機時，可能會變得很緊張。
冷靜溝通可幫助很緊張的人感到較安全。
應告訴對方已要求支援，並保持聯絡。

examples: No injuries, but one passenger is very anxious.
Very anxious means very worried, uneasy or frightened.
Someone who is very anxious may ask staff not to hang up.
A very anxious passenger needs calm reassurance and clear updates.
Do not dismiss anxiety; give safety instructions and stay in contact.
examples_zh: 沒有人受傷，但有一名乘客很焦慮。
Very anxious 是指非常擔心、不安或害怕。
很焦慮的人可能會要求職員不要掛線。
很焦慮的乘客需要冷靜安撫和清楚更新。
不要忽視焦慮；應給出安全指示並保持聯絡。

examples: Stay inside the lift.
Stay inside the lift means remain in the lift car and do not try to leave.
During lift entrapment, passengers should stay inside the lift.
Staying inside can be safer than trying to climb out.
Pair this instruction with “do not force the doors open.”
examples_zh: 請留在升降機內。
Stay inside the lift 是指留在升降機車廂內，不要嘗試離開。
升降機困人時，乘客應留在升降機內。
留在裏面可能比嘗試爬出更安全。
這句可配合「不要強行打開門」使用。

examples: Please remain inside and do not attempt to force the doors open.
Remain inside means stay where you are inside the lift or room.
Please remain inside until the responsible team arrives.
This phrase sounds calm and professional.
Use it when leaving the space may be unsafe.
examples_zh: 請留在裏面，不要嘗試強行打開門。
Remain inside 是指留在升降機或房間內的原處。
請留在裏面，直至負責團隊到達。
這句聽起來冷靜而專業。
當離開該空間可能不安全時，可使用這句。

examples: Do not attempt to force the doors open.
Attempt to means try to do something.
Do not attempt to leave the lift before help arrives.
Attempting to open the doors may create extra danger.
Use this phrase for actions people should not try during an emergency.
examples_zh: 不要嘗試強行打開門。
Attempt to 是指嘗試做某件事。
支援到達前，不要嘗試離開升降機。
嘗試打開門可能造成額外危險。
緊急情況下，可用這句說明人們不應嘗試的行動。

examples: I’m reporting the entrapment for urgent assistance now.
To report the entrapment means to inform the responsible team that people are trapped.
Report the entrapment with the lift number and number of passengers.
Reporting the entrapment quickly helps support reach the correct lift.
After reporting, stay in contact with the passengers if possible.
examples_zh: 我現在正匯報困人事件，要求緊急支援。
Report the entrapment 是通知負責團隊有人被困。
匯報困人事件時，應提供升降機編號和乘客人數。
迅速匯報困人事件，可幫助支援到達正確升降機。
匯報後，如情況許可，應與乘客保持聯絡。

examples: I’m reporting the entrapment for urgent assistance now.
Urgent assistance means help is needed quickly because the situation is serious.
Lift entrapment may require urgent assistance from the technical team.
Urgent assistance should be requested with accurate details.
Do not promise exactly when urgent assistance will arrive.
examples_zh: 我現在正匯報困人事件，要求緊急支援。
Urgent assistance 是指情況嚴重，需要快速支援。
升降機困人可能需要技術團隊提供緊急支援。
要求緊急支援時，應提供準確資料。
不要承諾緊急支援會在確實時間到達。

back: 讓我們出去；救我們出去
examples: How long will it take to get us out?
Get us out means rescue us or help us leave the trapped place.
Passengers in a stopped lift may ask when staff can get them out.
Staff should not guess the release time before assessment.
A safe answer explains that the responsible team must assess the lift first.
examples_zh: 要多久才可以救我們出去？
Get us out 是指救我們離開被困的地方。
停在半空的升降機內，乘客可能會問何時能救他們出去。
在評估前，職員不應猜測解困時間。
穩妥的回答應說明負責團隊需要先評估升降機。

examples: I’m unable to confirm a release time until the responsible team assesses the lift.
Release time means the time when trapped passengers can be freed.
Do not promise a release time before the lift is assessed.
A confirmed release time should come from the responsible team.
Use this phrase when passengers ask how long it will take.
examples_zh: 在負責團隊評估升降機前，我未能確認解困時間。
Release time 是指被困乘客可以獲救離開的時間。
升降機評估前，不要承諾解困時間。
已確認的解困時間應由負責團隊提供。
當乘客問需要多久時，可使用這個詞。

examples: The responsible team assesses the lift.
The responsible team is the group officially handling the problem.
For lift entrapment, the responsible team may include technical or lift maintenance staff.
Staff should wait for the responsible team before confirming release time.
This phrase helps explain why you cannot promise the result yourself.
examples_zh: 負責團隊會評估升降機。
負責團隊是正式處理問題的團隊。
升降機困人時，負責團隊可能包括技術或升降機維修人員。
職員應等待負責團隊確認後，才可說明解困時間。
這句可幫助解釋為何你不能自行承諾結果。

examples: The responsible team assesses the lift.
To assess the lift means to inspect the lift and decide what action is needed.
The technician must assess the lift before releasing passengers.
Assessing the lift helps prevent unsafe rescue attempts.
Use this phrase when explaining why time cannot yet be confirmed.
examples_zh: 負責團隊會評估升降機。
Assess the lift 是指檢查升降機並決定需要甚麼行動。
技術員必須先評估升降機，才讓乘客離開。
評估升降機有助避免不安全的救援嘗試。
解釋為何暫時不能確認時間時，可使用這句。

examples: Please don’t hang up.
Don’t hang up means do not end the phone or intercom call.
A nervous passenger may say, “Please don’t hang up.”
Staying connected can help reassure people during an entrapment.
Staff can answer, “I’ll stay in contact with you.”
examples_zh: 請不要掛線。
Don’t hang up 是指不要結束電話或對講機通話。
緊張的乘客可能會說：「請不要掛線。」
保持通話可在困人期間安撫對方。
職員可回答：「我會與您保持聯絡。」

examples: Can you stay on the intercom with us?
Stay on the intercom means keep talking through the building communication system.
Lift passengers may ask staff to stay on the intercom during entrapment.
The intercom helps staff receive updates from inside the lift.
Use this phrase when communication is through the lift system.
examples_zh: 你可以透過對講機與我們保持通話嗎？
Stay on the intercom 是指透過大廈通訊系統繼續通話。
升降機困人時，乘客可能會要求職員保持對講機通話。
對講機可幫助職員接收升降機內的最新情況。
透過升降機系統溝通時，可使用這句。

examples: Yes. I’ll maintain contact.
Maintain contact means continue communication without losing contact.
I’ll maintain contact until the responsible team arrives.
Maintaining contact helps staff monitor changes inside the lift.
This phrase sounds more professional than “I’ll stay here.”
examples_zh: 可以。我會保持聯絡。
Maintain contact 是指繼續溝通，不中斷聯絡。
我會保持聯絡，直至負責團隊到達。
保持聯絡可幫助職員留意升降機內的變化。
這句比 “I’ll stay here” 更專業。

examples: Please tell me immediately if anyone becomes unwell.
Becomes unwell means starts feeling sick, dizzy, weak or uncomfortable.
A passenger may become unwell if they are trapped for a long time.
Staff should ask for immediate updates if anyone becomes unwell.
This phrase helps monitor safety while help is being arranged.
examples_zh: 如果有人變得不適，請立即告訴我。
Becomes unwell 是指開始感到不舒服、頭暈、虛弱或不適。
如果被困時間較長，乘客可能會變得不適。
如果有人變得不適，職員應要求對方立即更新。
這句有助在安排支援期間監察安全。

examples: Please tell me immediately if the situation changes.
Situation changes means something new or different happens.
If the lift moves, the doors open, or someone feels unwell, the situation changes.
Reporting changes helps staff update the responding team.
Ask for immediate updates during any emergency.
examples_zh: 如果情況有變，請立即告訴我。
Situation changes 是指有新的或不同的事情發生。
如果升降機移動、門打開或有人不適，就是情況有變。
匯報變化可幫助職員更新到場處理團隊。
任何緊急情況中，都應要求立即更新。

examples: Suspicious Person in a Restricted Area.
A suspicious person is someone whose behaviour causes concern.
A person trying several office doors may be reported as suspicious.
Staff should ask for observed facts, not guesses about the person’s intention.
Keep a safe distance and report the exact location.
examples_zh: 限制區域出現可疑人士。
可疑人士是指行為令人擔心的人。
有人嘗試打開幾道辦公室門，可能會被匯報為可疑人士。
職員應查問可觀察事實，而不是猜測對方意圖。
應保持安全距離，並匯報確實位置。

examples: Suspicious Person in a Restricted Area.
A restricted area is a place where only authorised people may enter.
A staff-only corridor may be a restricted area.
If an unfamiliar person enters a restricted area, staff should report it.
Protect the restricted area without confronting the person yourself.
examples_zh: 限制區域出現可疑人士。
限制區域是只有獲授權人士可以進入的地方。
職員專用走廊可能是限制區域。
如果陌生人進入限制區域，職員應匯報。
應保護限制區域，但不要自行與對方對質。

examples: There is someone I don’t recognise near the corridor.
Don’t recognise means you do not know or identify the person.
A tenant may report someone they don’t recognise near an office door.
Not recognising someone does not prove wrongdoing, but it may require checking.
Staff should ask for location, behaviour and description.
examples_zh: 走廊附近有一個我不認識的人。
Don’t recognise 是指你不認識或不能辨認對方。
租戶可能會匯報辦公室門附近有不認識的人。
不認識某人不代表對方一定做錯事，但可能需要檢查。
職員應查問位置、行為和描述。

examples: There is someone I don’t recognise near the corridor.
Near the corridor means close to a passageway inside the building.
A suspicious person near the corridor should be reported with the exact floor.
Corridor information helps security find the person faster.
Ask which corridor if the floor has more than one.
examples_zh: 走廊附近有一個我不認識的人。
Near the corridor 是指靠近大廈內的通道。
走廊附近有可疑人士時，應同時匯報確實樓層。
走廊資料可幫助保安更快找到對方。
如果樓層有多條走廊，應查問是哪一條。

examples: He keeps trying different doors.
Trying different doors means attempting to open more than one door.
Someone trying different doors near offices may need security attention.
This behaviour should be reported as an observed fact.
Do not confront the person; keep a safe distance and report.
examples_zh: 他一直嘗試打開不同的門。
Trying different doors 是指嘗試打開多於一扇門。
有人在辦公室附近嘗試打開不同的門，可能需要保安注意。
這種行為應作為觀察到的事實匯報。
不要與對方對質；應保持安全距離並匯報。

examples: I’d like to report an unfamiliar person near a corridor.
An unfamiliar person is someone you do not know or do not usually see there.
A tenant may report an unfamiliar person near a staff-only access door.
The phrase is careful because it does not accuse the person of wrongdoing.
Ask what the unfamiliar person is doing now.
examples_zh: 我想匯報走廊附近有一名陌生人士。
陌生人士是指你不認識或平日不常在該處見到的人。
租戶可能會匯報職員專用出入口附近有陌生人士。
這個說法較謹慎，因為沒有指控對方做錯事。
應查問該陌生人士現在正在做甚麼。

examples: He appears to be trying several office doors.
Appears to be means something seems true based on observation.
The person appears to be checking door handles.
This phrase is useful when reporting carefully without overclaiming.
Use it with observable behaviour, not guesses about intention.
examples_zh: 他似乎正在嘗試打開幾道辦公室門。
Appears to be 是指根據觀察，某事似乎是真的。
那人似乎正在檢查門柄。
當你想謹慎匯報而不過分斷定時，這句很有用。
應用於可觀察行為，而不是猜測意圖。

examples: He appears to be trying several office doors.
Several office doors means more than two office doors.
A person checking several office doors may need security follow-up.
The number of doors can show whether the behaviour is repeated.
Report this fact clearly without adding personal guesses.
examples_zh: 他似乎正在嘗試打開幾道辦公室門。
Several office doors 是指多於兩道辦公室門。
有人檢查幾道辦公室門，可能需要保安跟進。
門的數量可顯示該行為是否重複。
應清楚匯報這項事實，不要加入個人猜測。

examples: Which floor and where exactly is the person?
Where exactly asks for the precise location.
“Near the pantry beside the rear service corridor” answers where exactly.
Exact location helps the security team respond faster.
Ask this before asking for clothing or appearance details.
examples_zh: 那人在哪一層？確實在哪裏？
Where exactly 是要求準確位置。
「在後勤服務走廊旁的茶水間附近」就是回答確實位置。
確實位置可幫助保安團隊更快回應。
應先問這句，再查問衣着或外貌資料。

examples: May I confirm the exact floor and corridor location first?
Corridor location means the specific corridor where the incident is happening.
“Rear service corridor beside the pantry” is a corridor location.
This helps security avoid searching the wrong corridor.
Use this phrase when several corridors exist on one floor.
examples_zh: 請問可否先確認確實樓層和走廊位置？
Corridor location 是指事故發生的具體走廊位置。
「茶水間旁的後勤服務走廊」就是走廊位置。
這可幫助保安避免搜尋錯誤走廊。
當同一樓層有多條走廊時，可使用這句。

examples: The person is at the rear service corridor beside the pantry.
A rear service corridor is a back corridor used mainly for service or staff movement.
A suspicious person in a rear service corridor should be reported clearly.
This location may be less visible than the main corridor.
Give nearby landmarks, such as the pantry or staff-only door.
examples_zh: 那人在茶水間旁邊的後勤服務走廊。
後勤服務走廊是主要供服務或職員通行的後方走廊。
後勤服務走廊出現可疑人士，應清楚匯報。
這個位置可能比主要走廊較不顯眼。
應提供附近地標，例如茶水間或職員專用門。

examples: The person is at the rear service corridor beside the pantry.
A pantry is a small area where staff may prepare drinks or simple food.
“Beside the pantry” is a useful landmark for locating someone.
If the exact room number is unknown, a pantry can help describe the area.
Mention the pantry only if it clearly helps identify the location.
examples_zh: 那人在茶水間旁邊的後勤服務走廊。
茶水間是職員準備飲品或簡單食物的小地方。
「茶水間旁邊」是定位某人的有用地標。
如果不知道確實房號，茶水間可幫助描述位置。
只有在茶水間有助清楚指出位置時，才應提及。

examples: The person is near the staff-only access door.
A staff-only access door is a door meant only for authorised staff.
Someone trying a staff-only access door may need security attention.
This phrase helps explain why the location is sensitive.
Report the door location, but do not confront the person yourself.
examples_zh: 那人在職員專用出入口附近。
職員專用出入口是只供獲授權職員使用的門。
有人嘗試打開職員專用出入口，可能需要保安注意。
這句有助解釋為何該位置較敏感。
應匯報該門位置，但不要自行與對方對質。

examples: What is the person doing now, and what do they look like?
What they look like asks for appearance details.
Clothing, bag colour and general appearance can help security identify the person.
Ask this after confirming the exact location.
Record only what the reporter can observe.
examples_zh: 那人現在正在做甚麼？對方外貌特徵如何？
What they look like 是查問外貌資料。
衣着、袋的顏色和大概外貌可幫助保安辨認對方。
應先確認確實位置，再問這句。
只記錄匯報者能觀察到的資料。

front: describe only what you can observe
back: 只描述你能觀察到的情況
examples: Could you describe only what you can observe?
This means report only what you can see or hear directly.
Describe clothing and behaviour, not personal guesses about motive.
This keeps the report factual and professional.
Use this phrase when a caller starts making assumptions.
examples_zh: 可否只描述你能觀察到的情況？
這是指只匯報你能直接看見或聽見的事情。
應描述衣着和行為，不要猜測動機。
這可令報告保持客觀和專業。
當來電者開始作出假設時，可使用這句。

examples: Could you describe their clothing?
Clothing means the clothes a person is wearing.
A dark jacket and black backpack are useful clothing details.
Clothing details help security identify the person without guessing.
Ask for clothing colour, type and any clear features.
examples_zh: 可否描述對方的衣着？
Clothing 是指一個人正在穿的衣服。
深色外套和黑色背囊都是有用的衣着資料。
衣着資料可幫助保安辨認對方，而不需要猜測。
可查問衣服顏色、類型和明顯特徵。

examples: Could you describe where they are standing?
Where they are standing asks for the person’s exact position now.
They are standing beside the pantry near the staff-only door.
This information helps the responding team approach the right area.
Ask again if the person starts moving.
examples_zh: 可否描述他們站在哪裏？
Where they are standing 是查問對方現在的確實位置。
他們站在茶水間旁邊，靠近職員專用門。
這項資料可幫助到場處理團隊前往正確範圍。
如果對方開始移動，應再次查問。

examples: He is wearing a dark jacket.
Wearing a dark jacket describes one visible clothing detail.
A dark jacket can help security identify the person in the corridor.
Clothing descriptions should be simple and factual.
Combine it with other details, such as backpack colour and location.
examples_zh: 他穿着深色外套。
Wearing a dark jacket 描述一項可見衣着資料。
深色外套可幫助保安在走廊辨認對方。
衣着描述應簡單而客觀。
可結合其他資料，例如背囊顏色和位置。

examples: He is carrying a backpack.
Carrying a backpack means the person has a backpack with them.
A backpack can be an identifying feature in a report.
Mention the backpack colour if it is visible.
Do not guess what is inside the backpack.
examples_zh: 他背着背囊。
Carrying a backpack 是指對方帶着背囊。
背囊可成為報告中的辨認特徵。
如果看得見，應提及背囊顏色。
不要猜測背囊裏有甚麼。

examples: He is carrying a black backpack.
A black backpack is a backpack that is black in colour.
“Black backpack” is a clear, observable detail.
This detail may help security distinguish the person from others.
Record colour only if the reporter can see it clearly.
examples_zh: 他背着黑色背囊。
Black backpack 是指黑色的背囊。
「黑色背囊」是清楚、可觀察的資料。
這項資料可幫助保安把該人與其他人區分。
只有在匯報者清楚看見時，才記錄顏色。

examples: He is still trying door handles.
Door handles are the parts used to open doors.
Trying door handles near offices may be suspicious behaviour.
This is an observable action, so it can be reported clearly.
Report which doors or corridor the handles are in if known.
examples_zh: 他仍在嘗試開門柄。
門柄是用來打開門的部件。
在辦公室附近嘗試開門柄，可能是可疑行為。
這是可觀察行動，因此可清楚匯報。
如知道，應匯報是哪些門或哪條走廊的門柄。

examples: He is checking several door handles.
Checking several door handles means testing more than one door handle.
This behaviour may suggest the person is trying to enter different rooms.
Report it as behaviour observed, not as a confirmed crime.
Staff should contact security and keep a safe distance.
examples_zh: 他正在檢查幾個門柄。
Checking several door handles 是指測試多個門柄。
這種行為可能顯示對方正在嘗試進入不同房間。
應把它作為觀察到的行為匯報，而不是確認罪行。
職員應聯絡保安，並保持安全距離。

examples: Please keep a safe distance and do not approach him.
Keep a safe distance means stay far enough away to avoid danger.
Keep a safe distance from an unfamiliar person near a restricted area.
This protects the reporter while security responds.
Use this instruction before telling the person to continue observing.
examples_zh: 請保持安全距離，不要接近他。
Keep a safe distance 是指保持足夠距離以避免危險。
對限制區域附近的陌生人士，應保持安全距離。
這可在保安回應期間保護匯報者。
要求對方繼續觀察前，應先給出這個指示。

examples: Please keep a safe distance and do not approach him.
Do not approach means do not go near the person.
If someone is acting suspiciously, do not approach them yourself.
Approaching the person may increase risk or cause confrontation.
Instead, report the location and description to security.
examples_zh: 請保持安全距離，不要接近他。
Do not approach 是指不要走近對方。
如果有人行為可疑，不要自行接近對方。
接近對方可能增加風險或引起衝突。
應改為向保安匯報位置和描述。

examples: Please do not approach or confront the person.
To confront the person means to challenge them directly or question them face to face.
Do not confront the person if they are near a restricted door.
Confrontation may make the situation more dangerous.
Let the security or management team handle the approach.
examples_zh: 請不要接近或與該人士對質。
Confront the person 是指正面挑戰或當面質問對方。
如果對方在限制區域門附近，不要與他對質。
對質可能令情況變得更危險。
應交由保安或管理團隊處理接觸。

examples: Stay in a secure area if possible.
A secure area is a safer place with controlled access or protection.
If you see a suspicious person, move to a secure area if possible.
Staying in a secure area protects the reporter while waiting for help.
Do not move there if doing so would bring you closer to danger.
examples_zh: 如情況許可，請留在安全範圍。
安全範圍是較安全、有出入控制或保護的地方。
如果看到可疑人士，如情況許可，應移到安全範圍。
留在安全範圍可在等候支援時保護匯報者。
如果移動會令你更接近危險，則不要前往。

examples: Stay in a secure area if possible.
If possible means if the situation allows it safely.
Continue to observe from a safe distance if possible.
This phrase avoids forcing someone to take an unsafe action.
Use it when the person’s safety depends on the situation.
examples_zh: 如情況許可，請留在安全範圍。
If possible 是指如果情況安全地容許。
如情況許可，請在安全距離外繼續觀察。
這句可避免強迫對方採取不安全行動。
當對方安全取決於現場情況時，可使用這句。

front: ask him what he is doing
examples: Should I ask him what he is doing?
To ask him what he is doing means to question the person directly about their actions.
Do not ask him what he is doing if it may lead to confrontation.
The safer action is to observe from a distance and report.
Staff should tell the reporter not to engage with him.
examples_zh: 我應該問他正在做甚麼嗎？
Ask him what he is doing 是指直接問對方正在做甚麼。
如果可能引起對質，便不要問他正在做甚麼。
較安全的做法是在遠處觀察並匯報。
職員應叫匯報者不要與他接觸或搭話。

examples: Should I speak to him or ask him to leave?
To ask him to leave means to tell the person to go away from the area.
A tenant should not ask a suspicious person to leave by themselves.
This may create confrontation or personal risk.
Security staff should handle the situation through proper procedures.
examples_zh: 我應該跟他說話，還是要求他離開？
Ask him to leave 是指叫對方離開該範圍。
租戶不應自行要求可疑人士離開。
這可能造成對質或個人風險。
保安人員應按正確程序處理情況。

examples: Please do not engage with him.
Do not engage with him means do not talk to, challenge or interact with him.
If a person is trying office doors, do not engage with him directly.
Avoiding engagement helps prevent the situation from escalating.
Report the facts and wait for the security team.
examples_zh: 請不要與他接觸或搭話。
Do not engage with him 是指不要與他說話、挑戰或互動。
如果有人嘗試打開辦公室門，不要直接與他接觸。
避免接觸可防止情況升級。
應匯報事實並等候保安團隊。

examples: I’ll report the exact location and description to the security / management team immediately.
The security or management team is responsible for handling safety and building incidents.
Suspicious-person reports should go to the security or management team.
Giving them clear facts helps them respond appropriately.
Tell the reporter the team has been informed when that is true.
examples_zh: 我會立即把確實位置和描述匯報給保安／管理團隊。
保安或管理團隊負責處理安全及大廈事故。
可疑人士報告應交給保安或管理團隊。
向他們提供清楚事實，可幫助他們作出合適回應。
當團隊已獲通知時，可告訴匯報者。

examples: I’ll report the exact location and description to the security / management team immediately.
Exact location and description means where the person is and what they look like or are doing.
“18/F, rear corridor, dark jacket, black backpack” gives location and description.
These details help security identify the correct person.
Keep the description factual and based on observation.
examples_zh: 我會立即把確實位置和描述匯報給保安／管理團隊。
確實位置及描述是指對方在哪裏，以及外貌或正在做甚麼。
「18樓，後方走廊，深色外套，黑色背囊」提供了位置和描述。
這些資料可幫助保安辨認正確人士。
描述應客觀，並根據觀察。

examples: He is walking towards the service lift now.
Walking towards means moving in the direction of a place or object.
The person is walking towards the staff-only access door.
Direction of movement helps the responding team track the person.
Update security immediately if the person changes direction.
examples_zh: 他現在正走向服務升降機。
Walking towards 是指朝某地方或物件的方向走。
那人正走向職員專用出入口。
移動方向可幫助到場處理團隊追蹤對方。
如果對方改變方向，應立即通知保安。

examples: He has just started walking towards the service lift.
A service lift is a lift often used by staff, contractors or for goods movement.
A suspicious person near the service lift should be reported with the exact floor.
Service lifts may be close to restricted or staff-only areas.
Mention the service lift if it helps locate the person.
examples_zh: 他剛開始走向服務升降機。
服務升降機通常供職員、承辦商或貨物運送使用。
服務升降機附近有可疑人士時，應同時匯報確實樓層。
服務升降機可能靠近限制區域或職員專用範圍。
如果有助定位，應提及服務升降機。

examples: Thank you for the update. Please continue to observe from a safe distance.
“Thank you for the update” acknowledges new information politely.
Use this phrase when the reporter tells you the person has moved.
It shows that the new information has been received.
After thanking them, give the next safety instruction.
examples_zh: 多謝您提供最新情況。請在安全距離外繼續觀察。
“Thank you for the update” 是有禮貌地確認收到新資料。
當匯報者告訴你對方已移動時，可使用這句。
這表示你已收到最新資料。
致謝後，應給出下一個安全指示。

examples: Please continue to observe from a safe distance.
Continue to observe means keep watching the situation carefully.
Continue to observe only if it is safe to do so.
Observing helps provide updates on the person’s location or behaviour.
Do not follow too closely or confront the person.
examples_zh: 請在安全距離外繼續觀察。
Continue to observe 是指繼續小心留意情況。
只有在安全情況下，才應繼續觀察。
觀察可提供對方位置或行為的更新。
不要太接近跟隨或與對方對質。

examples: Please continue to observe from a safe distance.
From a safe distance means far enough away to avoid danger.
Watch the person from a safe distance while the security team responds.
This protects the reporter and reduces the risk of confrontation.
Use this phrase when observation is useful but direct contact is unsafe.
examples_zh: 請在安全距離外繼續觀察。
From a safe distance 是指在足夠遠、可避免危險的位置。
保安團隊回應期間，請在安全距離外留意該人。
這可保護匯報者，並減少對質風險。
當觀察有用但直接接觸不安全時，可使用這句。

examples: Let us know immediately if his location or behaviour changes.
Let us know immediately means tell us right away.
Let us know immediately if the person moves towards another door.
Immediate updates help security respond to the latest situation.
Use this phrase when the situation may change quickly.
examples_zh: 如果他的位置或行為有變，請立即通知我們。
Let us know immediately 是指立刻告訴我們。
如果那人走向另一道門，請立即通知我們。
即時更新可幫助保安按最新情況回應。
當情況可能快速變化時，可使用這句。

examples: Let us know immediately if his location or behaviour changes.
Location or behaviour changes means the person moves or acts differently.
Walking towards the service lift is a location change.
Trying more doors is a behaviour change worth reporting.
These updates help the responding team track risk accurately.
examples_zh: 如果他的位置或行為有變，請立即通知我們。
位置或行為有變是指對方移動了，或行動變得不同。
走向服務升降機就是位置有變。
嘗試打開更多門是值得匯報的行為變化。
這些更新可幫助到場處理團隊準確追蹤風險。

examples: The responding team has been informed.
Responding team has been informed means the team that will handle the case has received the report.
The responding team has been informed of the exact location and description.
This phrase reassures the reporter that action is already being taken.
Use it only after the team has really been notified.
examples_zh: 已通知到場處理團隊。
Responding team has been informed 是指負責到場處理的團隊已收到報告。
已把確實位置和描述通知到場處理團隊。
這句可安撫匯報者，讓對方知道行動已在進行。
只有在真的已通知團隊後，才使用這句。
